ai.purpose: RTT structural map of the paper 'Thakur’s Hypotheses on Power Sums over F_q[t]'.
ai.module.summary: This module exposes the regime structure behind Thakur’s three hypotheses (H1–H3) on power sums over F_q[t], connecting carry-free combinatorics, Carlitz expansions, reciprocal slot geometry, and Sheats’ uniqueness theorem. It preserves the authors’ results while adding RTT operators for agentic reasoning.

carlitz_expansion_regime.description: Power sums Sd(k) expanded via Carlitz’s multinomial formula with carry-free constraints.
carlitz_expansion_regime.evidence: Section 3 uses Carlitz expansion (3) and Lucas’ theorem to characterize admissible decompositions.

greedy_assignment_regime.description: Prime-field H1 is solved by a weighted assignment problem with a unique greedy minimizer.
greedy_assignment_regime.evidence: Algorithm 3.3 and Lemma 3.4 show the greedy fill minimizes Φ.

reciprocal_slot_regime.description: H2 uses complementary digit-slot multisets and block minimization.
reciprocal_slot_regime.evidence: Theorem 5.1 expresses sd(k) via reciprocal blocks βr(k−1).

sheats_uniqueness_regime.description: H3 and the positive-power expansion rely on Sheats’ uniqueness of maximal weight decompositions.
sheats_uniqueness_regime.evidence: Lemma 4.4 and Theorem 4.2 ensure unique minimal exponent.

asymptotic_consequence_regime.description: Newton-polygon convexity, RH analogue, and multizeta nonvanishing follow from H2/H3.
asymptotic_consequence_regime.evidence: Corollaries 1.5–1.7 derive convexity, RH, and nonvanishing.

formalization_regime.description: Lean formalizations of H1–H3 generated by AxiomProver.
formalization_regime.evidence: Appendix describes Lean files and dependency graph.

digit_local_vs_degree_global.description: Local base-p digit constraints vs global degree of Sd(k).

prime_field_vs_extension_field.description: H1/H2 hold only for q=p; extension fields exhibit pathologies.
prime_field_vs_extension_field.paper_alignment: Examples in Appendix A.11 of [8] show failures for q=4.

combinatorial_vs_analytic_degree.description: Combinatorial digit assignments vs analytic consequences (RH, convexity).

positive_power_vs_negative_power_expansi.description: Carlitz expansion (negative powers) vs Sheats expansion (positive powers).
positive_power_vs_negative_power_expansi.paper_alignment: H1 uses Carlitz; H2/H3 use Lemma 4.1.

carlitz_to_greedy_transition.description: Translate Carlitz expansion into a weighted assignment problem.

digits_to_slots_transition.description: Convert base-p digits of k−1 into reciprocal slot multisets.

positive_power_to_uniqueness_transition.description: Use Sheats’ theorem to ensure unique minimal exponent.

recursion_to_convexity_transition.description: H2 recursion implies strict Newton-polygon convexity.

carlitz_operator.role: Expands Sd(k) via Carlitz multinomial formula and carry-free constraints.

greedy_assignment_operator.role: Computes the unique Φ-minimizing decomposition for H1.

reciprocal_slot_operator.role: Constructs Slotsp(k−1) and block sums βr(k−1).

block_minimization_operator.role: Applies block rearrangement inequality to derive H2 recursion.

sheats_operator.role: Applies Sheats’ uniqueness to positive-power expansions.

ai.audience: Researchers in finite-field arithmetic, zeta functions, combinatorics, and formal verification.
